# @arki/assert

> Two typed string checks, `isURL` and `isBase64`, one subpath each. They return a boolean and do not parse or decode.

## Import paths

<!-- llms:start -->
- `@arki/assert/base64`: Check that a string is standard base64 with correct `=` padding. `isBase64`.
- `@arki/assert/url`: Check that a string is an http or https URL with a host and a top-level domain. `isURL`.
<!-- llms:end -->

## Start here

- [Agent guide](docs/agent-guide.md): read first.
- [Verify](docs/agent-guide.md#verify): the commands to run after a change.

## By task

- [Check a URL a user typed](docs/agent-guide.md#check-a-url-a-user-typed)
- [Check a base64 secret before you decode it](docs/agent-guide.md#check-a-base64-secret-before-you-decode-it)
- [Validate a whole settings form](docs/agent-guide.md#validate-a-whole-settings-form)

## Rules that bite

- There is no root import. Use `@arki/assert/url` or `@arki/assert/base64`.
- `isBase64('')` is `true`. Check for an empty value yourself.
- `isURL` needs a protocol and a top-level domain. `localhost` fails.
- A non-string throws `TypeError` from `isBase64`. A bad string returns `false`.
